title: Deploy the development environment into chatticus-development
description:
First real environment in a new account, as the proving ground (per 2e4d79). ThinTurn, Web and Auth development plus the per-account shared stacks the app needs (Snapshots, Computers, Budgets). Start empty: new DynamoDB, new Cognito user pool, new queues; no data copied yet. Legacy development is not touched and keeps serving dev.chattic.us until cutover.

Needs: the bootstrap and deploy-role card, and the DNS decision. Also decide the account id the customer role template trusts (AnthusAccountId) for this environment, and set CHATTICUS_INSTALLATION_NAME and the budgets values for the account. Verify by a real sign-in and message on the new environment's own hostname before anything is repointed.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Started 2026-09-30 (Ryan: start the development deploy). Unblocked: deploy role and OIDC verified (911dac), zone moved to the management account (4e4819 steps 1-4). PLAN from a read-only survey of the stacks:

FINDINGS
- The legacy design gives Web and Auth ONE shared hosted zone and ONE wildcard certificate (chattic.us, *.chattic.us, www) from ChatticusDns. That cannot exist across accounts: a wildcard's validation record lives at the top of chattic.us, in the management zone. Per the delegation decision each environment account needs its own small zones and certificates for ITS names: for development two zones (dev.chattic.us for Web, auth-dev.chattic.us for Auth), each certificate validated inside its own delegated zone, plus NS delegation records in the management zone. Cognito's custom domain also needs an A record on the parent domain chattic.us, which the management zone has (marketing apex).
- CloudFront alternate domain names and Cognito custom domains are unique WORLDWIDE. A second distribution cannot claim dev.chattic.us while legacy development still holds it, so the new environment cannot use the real hostnames until legacy releases them.
- What a person must seed in a new account: the Google OAuth secret chatticus/development/oauth/google (read at DEPLOY time by the auth stack, so it must exist before it deploys) and its redirect URIs; the OpenAI key as an SSM SecureString /chatticus/development/thin-turn/openai-api-key (read at RUNTIME only, deploy does not need it; a dedicated OpenAI project per deployment per BUDGETS.md). ThinTurn itself needs no seeds to deploy.
- Every environment account needs its own copies of the shared stacks (Budgets, Snapshots, Computers); each environment account becomes the account that customers trust (AnthusAccountId is the account running that environment's workers, which is natural).

CODE WORK (IaC only, Gherkin/tests first)
1. An account mode for the CDK app, -c chatticusAccountEnvironment=development, that builds only that environment's stacks plus its own shared stacks, and leaves the legacy three-environment default untouched.
2. An environment DNS stack: the two delegated zones and their certificates; Web and Auth get their own zone and certificate (today they share one).
3. Hostnames come from configuration (context) instead of being fixed per environment, one code path.

PROVING THEN CUTOVER (recommended): deploy first under temporary hostnames (dev2.chattic.us and auth-dev2.chattic.us) delegated to the dev account, verify a real sign-in and message there, and only then cut over to the real names after legacy releases them. Dev downtime at that moment is acceptable.

NEEDS RYAN: (1) agree the dev2 proving hostnames; (2) a monthly budget amount for the new dev account (the  whole-account number does not apply); (3) a dedicated OpenAI project key and the Google OAuth secret and redirect URIs, seeded by Ryan in the dev account with his own SSO session so the values never pass through an agent; exact commands will be provided.

comments.text: 2026-09-30: Ryan chose the hostname 'develop' (read as: develop.chattic.us and auth-develop.chattic.us as the development environment's permanent names, which also removes the proving-then-rename step; legacy's dev.chattic.us is simply retired with legacy). PR #378 implements the code half, nothing deployed yet: -c chatticusAccountEnvironment=ENV builds one environment's stacks plus its own shared stacks; ChatticusEnvironmentZones (two delegated zones) and ChatticusEnvironmentCertificates (one certificate per name, validated in its own zone; separate from the zones because validation cannot finish before the NS delegation exists); hostnames are explicit inputs to web, auth and the web build; guarded deploy-chatticus-dedicated-account.sh (refuses the legacy account). Legacy verified unchanged: 13 of 13 legacy templates byte-identical against a clean develop worktree. DEPLOY ORDER (infra/README.md): budgets, snapshots, computers; zones; delegate both names from the management zone (a reviewed change to ChatticusManagementDns) and wait for dig; certificates; thin-turn; PERSON seeds the Google OAuth secret chatticus/development/oauth/google and the OpenAI key in the dev account with their own SSO session; then auth; then web (web build reads the Cognito ids auth publishes). STILL NEEDED FROM RYAN: a monthly budget amount for the new dev account (question 2), and the two secrets (question 3). Google OAuth redirect URIs must include https://auth-develop.chattic.us/oauth2/idpresponse.

comments.text: 2026-10-01: #378 merged (a338ae9). DEPLOYED to chatticus-development (guarded script, development credentials, not legacy): ChatticusSnapshots, ChatticusComputers (VPC with NO NAT gateways, empty ECR repo, Fargate service at desired count 0), ChatticusEnvironmentZones. Verified: two delegated zones develop.chattic.us and auth-develop.chattic.us each holding only NS and SOA, stacks tagged chatticus:environment=development (so the dedicated-account tag override works), nothing deployed with legacy credentials. Delegation is PR #379 (NS records in ChatticusManagementDns as reviewed IaC; committed name servers verified equal to the live zones). NEXT: merge #379, deploy ChatticusManagementDns once from the management session, dig both names through public resolvers, then deploy ChatticusEnvironmentCertificates, then ChatticusThinTurn. BLOCKED ON RYAN for Auth and Web: the Google OAuth secret and OpenAI key seeded from his own session (exact commands to follow), the Google redirect URI https://auth-develop.chattic.us/oauth2/idpresponse, and a budget amount for the new account (ChatticusBudgets not deployed yet). Housekeeping noted: dedicated-account deploys write account-specific availability-zone lookups into the tracked infra/cdk.context.json in the working tree; restore it, never commit it.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-01 PROGRESS. #379 merged (04d4e6e); ChatticusManagementDns redeployed from the management session after a cdk diff showed exactly two NS records added and nothing else. DELEGATION VERIFIED end to end: the management zone's own server delegates develop.chattic.us and auth-develop.chattic.us to the dev-account name servers; Google, Cloudflare and Quad9 all reach the dev-account zones (SOA names the dev zones); existing sites (apex, dev, hey) still 200. DEPLOYED to chatticus-development with the guarded script and development credentials: ChatticusEnvironmentCertificates (both certificates ISSUED, validation CNAMEs created inside each name's own delegated zone, InUse 0) and ChatticusThinTurn (front door /health 200, an authenticated route 403 with no credential, DynamoDB table, two queues, five Lambdas, SSM parameters; no rollup Lambda yet because Budgets is not deployed). The OpenAI parameter is absent as expected. REMAINING: (1) Ryan seeds the Google OAuth secret chatticus/development/oauth/google as JSON {client_id, client_secret} and adds https://auth-develop.chattic.us/oauth2/idpresponse to the Google OAuth client's authorized redirect URIs; (2) Ryan seeds the OpenAI SecureString /chatticus/development/thin-turn/openai-api-key; (3) I deploy auth then web; (4) verify a real sign-in and a message on https://develop.chattic.us; (5) a budget amount from Ryan, then deploy ChatticusBudgets and redeploy ThinTurn so the rollup Lambda exists; (6) follow-up: the dedicated-account script does not pass the ECS host-start context that the legacy ThinTurn script reads from ChatticusComputers, so computer hosts cannot start in the new account yet (computerCount is 0 and no image is pushed, so nothing needs it today).

Cognito question resolved by Ryan (broker-only Google sign-in, separate pool per product, no managed users) and verified: the app sends identity_provider=Google, and the hosted Cognito page reached directly has no forms and no username/password inputs, only a Google button. REMAINING for this card's done-when (a real sign-in and message on the new hostname): Ryan signs in with Google at https://develop.chattic.us (a new account has no organization, signup mode is open so he creates one), and seeds the OpenAI SecureString /chatticus/development/thin-turn/openai-api-key so a message can be answered. comments.author: home
comments.text: DONE 2026-10-01. VERIFIED END TO END on https://develop.chattic.us, driven in the browser pane with Ryan: Sign in with Google goes straight to Google's account chooser (redirect auth-develop.chattic.us/oauth2/idpresponse, no Cognito page, no username/password anywhere), Ryan picked ryan@anth.us, landed on the app signed in; the new pool holds one EXTERNAL_PROVIDER stub and zero native users. A newly created organization is 'pending' (the customer path asks for an AWS account id and role); the operator step python -m chatticus.members enable (status only, no computer) enabled 'Anthus AI Solutions' in the DEV account only; the workspace then opened, a bot 'Ping' was created through the UI, a message sent, and Ping answered via OpenAI ('Hello from the new development account-nice to meet you!'), stored in the dev account's own DynamoDB. In chatticus-development: ChatticusSnapshots, Computers (no NAT gateways, desired count 0), EnvironmentZones, EnvironmentCertificates (both issued), ThinTurn, Auth, Web; delegation in ChatticusManagementDns; AccountDeploy role verified by OIDC earlier. NOT in this card (filed or already carded): GitHub cutover and legacy dev retirement (c649bf), staging and production (7ebd57), tenant cost tag and the member-account tag check (d706d7, 309a7e), ECS host-start context, the budget for the new account. Legacy was never touched.

right_now_summary: The new development environment is live and verified; budget setup, GitHub cutover, and legacy retirement remain.
